races.paceDynamic: Jolly Good Fellows will dictate from the front with no other confirmed speed horses, creating a controlled tempo early. The prominent runners Sovereign Glory, Super Tuscan, Seed Ya Later and Passerine will track behind but none are aggressive early types. With limited pace pressure, Jolly Good Fellows can set sustainable fractions and kick clear in the straight. This setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jolly Good Fellows Repeats
scenarios.trigger: If Jolly Good Fellows gets an uncontested lead and sets her own fractions
scenarios.body: She can dictate terms from flag to finish and prove too strong late, replicating last week's victory. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to conserve energy for a decisive move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners track closer than expected and put pressure on the leader
scenarios.body: Seed Ya Later or Sovereign Glory can strike from ideal positions behind the pace-setter. Their superior ratings advantage tells in a sustained drive to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Suits Holdups
scenarios.trigger: If Jolly Good Fellows sets an overly pedestrian tempo that becomes tactical
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where Our Fella's unknown ability could emerge. A slowly-run race neutralizes the front-runner's advantage and opens up possibilities.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Folds Under Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Jolly Good Fellows simultaneously from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The pace-setter's limitations show as she's swamped by better-rated rivals. Super Tuscan could benefit from the strong pace having shown early speed before.

watchPoints.text: Jolly Good Fellows faces the risk of a quick turnaround after just 8 days since her last victory
Super Tuscan's early speed could disrupt the expected scenario if he presses Jolly Good Fellows early
Our Fella's debut for highly-rated connections could spring a surprise given his unknown ability
Track conditions showing Good To Firm across all distances favours the proven course performers
The lack of genuine early pace beyond Jolly Good Fellows could create a falsely-run race

races.paceDynamic: Candy Warhol and Under Curfew are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead in this small field of eight. With seven hold-up horses behind them, the pace is likely to be honest but not suicidal, as the two leaders may not need to go flat out early. The absence of prominent runners means a clear gap between the front pair and the rest, creating a tactical race where those able to track the leaders closely will have an advantage. This race shape strongly favours horses with enough pace to position prominently or those who can quicken effectively from midfield, rather than genuine hold-up horses who may get too far behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-runners dominate field
scenarios.trigger: If Candy Warhol and Under Curfew set sensible fractions without killing each other
scenarios.body: The honest gallop suits their stamina while seven hold-up horses leave themselves too much to do from the rear. The leaders get first run and prove hard to peg back over this sharp 5½f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses storm home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong between the two front-runners or they go too slow early
scenarios.body: Either a hot pace sets up the closers perfectly or a slow pace allows them to use their turn of foot. The class horses from the rear get the perfect setup to unleash late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse favours positioning
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners fold tamely leaving a tactical finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole with those best positioned to strike. Horses who can track the pace without being trapped wide benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos creates surprise winner
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems or interference disrupt the fancied runners' passages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where gate position and luck in running matter more than ability. An outsider who gets a clear run benefits from others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Candy Warhol and Under Curfew go too fast early, as this could set up a dramatic late charge from the hold-up horses
Monitor Hidden Verse's positioning through the race as he needs to be closer than usual on this sharp track to be effective
Keep an eye on Danger Alert who returns from a long break with cheekpieces and a dropping handicap mark
Watch for traffic problems in the straight as six hold-up horses will all be looking for racing room simultaneously
Observe if Under Curfew shows the same front-running tactics as usual or drops back like he did at Windsor last time

races.paceDynamic: Queen Sana will take the lead from the break and dictate throughout, with no other committed front-runners to challenge her early. In The City will track just behind in second, while Noble Vow and Princess Of Limnos settle further back. The pace will be controlled rather than frantic, allowing Queen Sana to string the field out down the back straight before the final sprint unfolds. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and hold-up horses who get a true test of stamina, as the sustained gallop will find out the pure speed merchants.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Sana maintains her lead without being seriously challenged until the final furlong
scenarios.body: The even tempo allows her to kick again when threatened, while In The City gets first run from his tracking position. Both prominent runners benefit from the lack of early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace sets up a strong late kick from the back markers
scenarios.body: Noble Vow overcomes his pulling tendencies by settling better, while the sustained gallop brings stamina into play. The hold-up horses get the perfect scenario with plenty left in the tank.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Sana ties up after her recent quick return or gets pressured more than expected
scenarios.body: In The City inherits the lead and has enough left to repel late challengers, benefiting from his patient tactics. The race falls apart for connections between leader and closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Debut Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Far From Fern shows significantly more ability than his breeding suggests and benefits from the race dynamics
scenarios.body: The newcomer finds the sustained pace ideal for a staying type making his debut, while the exposed runners fail to capitalize. Professional debut rides sometimes spring surprises in weak maidens.

watchPoints.text: Noble Vow settling early behind the pace rather than fighting Pat Dobbs, as his recent pulling habits have compromised his finishing kick.
Queen Sana's jumping and early pace-setting, as any hesitation from the gates allows In The City to take closer order.
In The City's fitness levels after 293 days off, particularly whether he can sustain his challenge in the final furlong.
Far From Fern's market moves and early positioning, as any confidence or ability shown could signal future potential.
Princess Of Limnos staying on in the final stages rather than fading, which would represent significant improvement from previous efforts.

races.paceDynamic: Hibernate will take them along from the front after winning by dictating the pace at Yarmouth, with Electric Bass, and Bobby Dassler likely to sit prominently behind him in this small field. Raintown will track from the rear as the only confirmed hold-up performer. With just one natural leader and three prominent runners not applying immediate pressure, this sets up a steady tempo that will quicken late. This pace scenario strongly favors the hold-up horse Raintown, who can use his finishing kick when the race develops into a sprint from the back of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Raintown Kicks Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate sets modest fractions without serious pressure from the prominent trio.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a staying test where Raintown's fresh legs and hold-up style prove decisive in the final two furlongs. David Probert can time his challenge perfectly as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate maintains his Yarmouth form and gets easy sectionals on the front end.
scenarios.body: The leader kicks clear approaching the final furlong as the small field fails to mount a serious challenge to his sustained pace. Rossa Ryan repeats the front-running tactics that worked perfectly last time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Bass or Bobby Dassler press Hibernate early and force stronger sectionals.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens significantly with multiple horses vying for position, setting up a driving finish between the prominent runners. Jack Mitchell or Christian Howarth capitalize on their forward positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all three prominent runners get into an early speed duel pressuring Hibernate.
scenarios.body: The tempo becomes unsustainably fast through the middle sections, allowing Raintown to sweep past tired leaders. The small field works against itself with too much early pace.

watchPoints.text: Hibernate's ability to handle the 9lb swing from his claiming win will determine if he can repeat his front-running dominance
Electric Bass breaking his maiden tag after 12 attempts if the pace setup allows him to strike from his prominent position
Raintown's fitness levels second time back after three months off, having needed his recent Bath comeback run
Bobby Dassler's course advantage and 80-1 runner-up form here last week making him dangerous at big odds again
The small field creating tactical complications where one horse could potentially steal a march on the others

races.paceDynamic: Prodigal Son will take this field along as the sole natural front runner, with no other pace pressure allowing him to dictate fractions. The four hold-up horses (Criminal, Party Island, Premier, Galaxy Wonder) will all settle behind in a bunched group, creating a compressed field through the middle stages. This small field dynamic with uncontested leadership sets up a tactical battle where the front runner can control the tempo completely. This race shape strongly favours the front runner profile, as Prodigal Son can steal a march without pace pressure and make his stamina concerns irrelevant.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prodigal Son Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Prodigal Son gets soft fractions and kicks clear approaching the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to save energy early and have enough left to resist the late challenge. His tactical advantage from controlling the tempo outweighs stamina doubts over this longer trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade gets into a rhythm and Prodigal Son stops in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Galaxy Wonder and Party Island time their runs perfectly as the leader's stamina gives way. The compressed field behind unleashes multiple challengers who overwhelm the tiring front runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Criminal's Headgear Impact
scenarios.trigger: If Criminal's first-time headgear transforms his effort and he gets a dream trip
scenarios.body: The headgear sharpens his focus dramatically and he finds the turn of foot that's been missing. His recent AW near-miss form translates perfectly to this tactical scenario under the new setup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Premier Returns Fresh
scenarios.trigger: If Premier's 252-day break and wind surgery prove significantly beneficial
scenarios.body: His class edge shows through after the long rest and wind operation, making up for ring rustiness with raw ability. The tactical pace setup suits his hold-up style perfectly as he storms home late.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Prodigal Son gets any early pressure from the hold-up horses trying to sit closer, as this would compromise his tactical advantage completely
Watch Criminal's early behaviour with first-time headgear as any settling issues could ruin his chances in this small tactical field
Watch Premier for signs of fitness after 252 days off, as any ring rustiness will be exposed in this pace setup
Watch the pace through the middle stages as the bunched hold-up quartet could create interference problems turning for home
Watch Galaxy Wonder's position turning in as his hat-trick bid depends on finding clear running room from his hold-up style

races.paceDynamic: Kondratiev Wave is the lone confirmed front runner and will likely dictate terms from the start without serious pressure. The majority of the field are hold-up horses (Thapa Vc, Racing Demon, Nammos, Lady Of The Isles, My Ambition, Havana Club, Purple Sky, Rovinia, Vecchio) who will sit off the pace and rely on late runs. With only one genuine pace-setter and a cluster of closers, this creates a tactical disadvantage for the hold-up brigade who may find themselves with too much ground to make up if Kondratiev Wave gets loose on the lead. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and the lone front runner, as the lack of early pace pressure allows them to control the tempo and kick clear when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave gets an uncontested lead and dictates soft fractions.
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old can use his tactical advantage to control the race and prove too strong for the hold-up horses who face a difficult task from off the pace. His string of good AW form translates well to this tactical scenario where he holds all the cards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses can get close enough to mount a serious challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Despite the tactical disadvantage, class horses like My Ambition and Thapa Vc could use their superior ability to reel in the leader if he goes too slow early. The C&D experience of My Ambition becomes crucial in this grinding finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lesser-fancied hold-up horses produces a career-best effort.
scenarios.body: Havana Club showed real promise when just a head behind here last time despite a slow start, and without the hood he could time his run perfectly. Racing Demon's C&D wins and return to his favoured 1m trip could see him overcome his slow-start habit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave goes too fast early or stops quickly, creating a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: The front runner's tactics backfire and the race becomes a lottery among the hold-up horses, with any of them capable of picking up the pieces. Form and class go out the window in a messy sprint finish where positioning proves decisive.

watchPoints.text: Kondratiev Wave breaking clear early and getting uncontested fractions - if he leads by 3+ lengths turning for home he'll be very hard to catch
My Ambition and Thapa Vc getting squeezed for racing room in the straight as multiple hold-up horses look for the same gap
Racing Demon's starting position from the stalls - his slow-start habit becomes even more costly in a race lacking early pace
Havana Club's early positioning without the hood - previous slow starts have cost him but removal of headgear might help his alertness
The pace through the first half-mile - if Kondratiev Wave goes too steadily the hold-up horses get a better chance, if he goes too fast he's vulnerable late
